text:
Ryan (CTO): Thanks everyone for the runtime section today. Opening this thread for quick clarifying Qs and follow-ups about batching/caching/kernel work. Drop short items and we'll triage.
Sophie (Runtime Eng): TL;DR: core things we'll doc: batching heuristics, fallback order, KV cache eviction policies, kernel affinity notes.
Jules (EngOps): Can we get an explicit metric set that triggers autoshrink vs hold batch? e.g., p95 queue wait > X ms && throughput < Y -> shrink?
Sophie (Runtime Eng): Proposed signals: p95 queue-wait, inter-arrival percentile (p50), current pool utilization, route SLO tag. We'll publish thresholds but they will be tunable per-customer.
Nina (SRE): Ops question: when kernel JIT happens, does it block other requests on the same GPU? We saw a small spike during a test.
Kai (Kernel): JIT is per-process and can momentarily increase latency for concurrent in-flight work if the CUDA context is busy. We're adding async JIT threading and pre-warm cache propagation to mitigate.
Maya (Product): Product ask: simplest UX to represent this in Console? thinking: per-route toggle + SLO slider (latency vs throughput) + "advanced" to edit thresholds.
Ryan (CTO): That maps well to the runtime signals. Sophie/Kai: can we prepare a one-pager mapping Console UX -> runtime signals & fallback actions?
Sophie (Runtime Eng): Yep. I'll draft it.
Jules (EngOps): On kernel-affinity: does it require dedicated pools per seq-len bracket or can it be soft-affinity?
Kai (Kernel): Soft-affinity is preferred: bins for seq ranges and soft-pinning. Hard partitions hurt utilization. We plan soft bins with migration heuristics.
Anonymous: For dedicated customers, will we surface cost/latency tradeoffs for recommended quantization?
Maya (Product): Yes, Optimize will show estimated cost delta and a sample diff for representative prompts. Auto-apply remains opt-in.
Sophie (Runtime Eng): Note on caching: prefix/KV cache eviction will be LRU by default but we also plan a hotspot-aware TTL option to avoid cache pollution from noisy short-lived keys.
Nina (SRE): Action: run a canary with new fused-attn kernel + pre-warm across 3 nodes and monitor p99/jit spikes. I'll schedule.
Jules (EngOps): Can someone paste an example route YAML snippet that maps UX toggles to runtime config? small one for runbooks please.
Sophie (Runtime Eng): Paste minimal example:
```yaml
route: /generate/low-latency
slo: latency
batching:
  max_wait_ms: 10
  max_batch_tokens: 1024
  affinity: soft
fallbacks:
  - kernel_swap
  - reduce_batch_window: true
  - model_variant: quant-8
caching:
  kv_cache: enabled
  eviction: hotspot-aware-lru
```
Jules (EngOps): Perfect, adding to runbook.
Ryan (CTO): OK next steps: Sophie to publish the one-pager + YAML examples; Kai to post kernel-affinity design and microbench table; Nina to schedule canary and share monitoring checklist; Maya to confirm Console flag timeline. Followup-bot: please create tracker items.
followup-bot: Created follow-ups: runtime-onepager (Sophie), kernel-affinity-microbench (Kai), canary-fused-attn (Nina), console-slo-ux (Maya).
Maya (Product): Timeline: feature-flagged Console controls in ~6 weeks, beta to select customers in ~9.
Kai (Kernel): Microbench table coming tomorrow to #kernel.
Sophie (Runtime Eng): I'll push the one-pager PR by Friday.
Ryan (CTO): Thanks. If there are more small Qs, drop here. We'll fold into the public FAQ and link from the all-hands notes. :thumbsup:
